tags: Boxed warning: Concomitant opioid use; abuse, misuse, addiction; dependence and withdrawal
quick: GAD 0.25-0.5 mg TID; PD 0.5 mg TID (max 4 mg/day GAD)
Risk of neonatal sedation/withdrawal; avoid unless necessary
Start 0.25 mg 2-3 times daily; reduce dose
Avoid - additive CNS depression, may be fatal
summary: Alprazolam is a short-acting benzodiazepine indicated for acute treatment of generalized anxiety disorder and for panic disorder in adults. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance and is habit forming, carrying a boxed warning for risks with concomitant opioids, abuse/misuse/addiction, and dependence/withdrawal. Use lowest effective dose for the shortest duration and taper to discontinue.
indications: Acute treatment of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) in adults
Treatment of panic disorder (PD), with or without agoraphobia, in adults

dosage.d: Starting 0.25 mg to 0.5 mg three times daily; maximum 4 mg/day in divided doses
dosage.n: May adjust every 3 to 4 days; use lowest effective dose and reassess need

dosage.d: Starting 0.5 mg three times daily; increase by no more than 1 mg/day
dosage.n: Trials used 1-10 mg/day (mean ~5-6 mg/day); reassess and consider reduction above 4 mg/day
Increase gradually if tolerated; reduce dose if adverse reactions occur

dosage.d: Decrease by no more than 0.5 mg every 3 days
dosage.n: Some patients require a slower taper; pause or raise dose if withdrawal occurs

admin: Administer orally; may be taken with or without food
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
Assess risk for abuse, misuse, and addiction before and during treatment
Do not discontinue abruptly - taper gradually to avoid withdrawal
Avoid concomitant opioids unless no alternative; if combined, limit dose/duration and monitor
moa: Alprazolam is a 1,4-benzodiazepine. It binds to the benzodiazepine site of gamma-aminobutyric acid-A (GABA-A) receptors in the brain and enhances GABA-mediated synaptic inhibition.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to alprazolam or other benzodiazepines (angioedema reported)
Concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), except ritonavir
relative: History of substance abuse or addiction
monitor: Respiratory depression and sedation, especially with opioids/CNS depressants

preg: Neonates born to mothers using benzodiazepines late in pregnancy have been reported to experience sedation and/or neonatal withdrawal. Available observational data do not report a clear association with major birth defects. Avoid unless clearly needed; weigh maternal benefit against neonatal risk. A pregnancy exposure registry exists for psychiatric medications (1-866-961-2388).
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with alprazolam.
hepatic: Reduced clearance and prolonged elimination half-life occur in hepatic impairment (e.g., ~19.7 hours in alcoholic liver disease vs ~11.4 hours in healthy subjects). Recommended starting dose is 0.25 mg given 2 or 3 times daily, increased gradually if tolerated; dosage reduction is recommended.

major: Opioids - profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death; limit dose/duration and monitor
Strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole) - contraindicated (except ritonavir); increased alprazolam exposure
Other CNS depressants and alcohol - additive depression, may be fatal
moderate: Digoxin - increased risk of digoxin toxicity
Ritonavir - alters alprazolam levels; dosage adjustment needed
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid grapefruit (CYP3A inhibition can raise levels).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; combination causes additive CNS depression and may be fatal.

emergency: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, or coma

monitoring: Respiratory depression and sedation, especially with concomitant opioids or CNS depressants
Signs of abuse, misuse, and addiction throughout treatment
Withdrawal reactions during taper or dosage reduction
Continued need for treatment and lowest effective dose
counsel: This medicine is habit forming; take exactly as prescribed and do not increase dose on your own
Do not use with opioids or alcohol unless directed - risk of severe sedation and death
Do not stop suddenly; the dose must be tapered to avoid withdrawal
May impair driving and operating machinery; avoid until effects are known
Store securely to prevent misuse or diversion
Tell your clinician if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding
Report excessive drowsiness or trouble breathing immediately
pk: Peak plasma concentration in 1 to 2 hours
About 11.2 hours (range 6.3 to 26.9) in healthy adults
Store per product labeling at controlled room temperature
pearls: Schedule IV controlled substance; habit forming with risk of dependence even at therapeutic doses
Extensively metabolized by CYP3A4 - strong inhibitors are contraindicated (except ritonavir)
Abrupt discontinuation can cause life-threatening withdrawal; always taper
Geriatric and hepatic patients have reduced clearance - start at 0.25 mg
Flumazenil reverses sedation but is not first-line and can precipitate withdrawal/seizures
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose, in which case skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. Because alprazolam is habit forming, do not change the dosing schedule without medical advice.
overdose: Overdose causes CNS depression ranging from drowsiness, confusion, dysarthria, lethargy, diminished reflexes, ataxia, and hypotonia to respiratory depression and coma; rarely paradoxical disinhibition. Combination with other CNS depressants, alcohol, or opioids may be fatal. Provide supportive care with IV fluids and airway management. Flumazenil may be used to reverse sedation but can precipitate withdrawal/seizures. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
